national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Agence du revenu du Canada, administering federal corporate income tax and GST/HST through the 'My Business Account' portal; Revenu Québec - Revenue Québec, administering Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and Quebec corporate tax through 'Mon dossier d'entreprise'; Registraire des entreprises du Québec for mandatory enterprise registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first determine whether it carries on business in Canada. If required to register, the entity obtains a CRA Business Number (BN) as the statutory tax identifier. Application is made through CRA Business Registration Online, by telephone, by mail, or through a Canadian agent; a non-resident corporation may be issued a non-resident GST/HST program account under the BN. In Quebec, the entity must also obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) through the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and register for QST with Revenu Québec. For a domestically incorporated Business Corporation, the registration process is triggered at incorporation: the Registraire or Corporations Canada creates the entity record, CRA assigns the BN, and the taxpayer activates the corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and import/export program accounts as needed. Registration is mandatory when taxable supplies exceed the applicable CAD 30,000 threshold, regardless of foreign or domestic status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a 'check-the-box' election system. A Business Corporation formed under Canadian or Quebec law is automatically a separate entity taxed at the corporate level under Part I of the Income Tax Act and, in Quebec, under the Taxation Act. Hybrid entity and hybrid mismatch arrangements are addressed by Canadian domestic classification principles and by the anti-hybrid deduction-denial provisions in the Income Tax Act; no elective reclassification for foreign-tax purposes is available. Other elections, such as functional-currency reporting under section 261 or the non-resident section 216 election, do not alter entity-level corporate taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal VAT-type consumption tax) and Quebec Sales Tax / Taxe de vente du Québec (QST) (provincial VAT-type consumption tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in the last four consecutive calendar quarters for GST/HST registration; CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Quebec in the last four consecutive calendar quarters for QST registration. Once exceeded, registration is mandatory from the next transaction unless the small-supplier exception applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-based pre-approval, or digital stamping of invoices. Electronically issued and archived invoices are valid if they contain prescribed information: supplier legal name, Business Number/QST registration number, date, description, amount, and tax charged. Systems such as Peppol or private EDI portals are permitted but are voluntary. CRA and Revenu Québec rely on post-audit document review and mandatory record retention rather than prepayment invoice clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of bulk pharmaceutical API goods qualifies for 0% GST/HST and QST where the supplier retains contemporaneous evidence that the goods were exported by the supplier or by an unregistered recipient, delivered outside Canada as soon as practicality permits, and not consumed or resold in Canada. Services supplied to non-residents qualify for zero-rating when the services are performed or delivered outside Canada and are not in connection with Canadian real property or goods; the claimant must establish the non-resident status of the recipient and the export nature of the supply under the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec QST rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA / Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13) or equivalent Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) electronic export report
Commercial Invoice containing full API trade description, quantity, unit value, and Incoterms
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Cargo Manifest issued by the carrying carrier
Proof of Export from the carrier, terminal, customs broker, or port authority
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103 / wire confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Certificate of Origin or preferential tariff document where applicable
Export permit, Health Canada authorization, or controlled substances licence where the pharmaceutical API classification requires regulatory approval
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess a zero-rated export claim and reverse the zero rating if the documentary export trail is incomplete, the payment is not repatriated within the prescribed deadline, or the transaction is found to lack a genuine commercial export purpose. Reassessment may occur within the normal limitation period, with no limitation period where misrepresentation or fraud is established. Reversed claims become taxable, the taxpayer must remit GST and QST together with interest, and civil penalties may include gross-negligence penalties under the Excise Tax Act and corresponding Quebec penalty provisions. Directors and officers may incur personal liability for unremitted or clawed-back GST/HST and QST, and criminal prosecution for false statements or wilful evasion can result in fines and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), constituted under the Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. B-2), acts as the central bank, operator of the Lynx large-value real-time gross settlement (RTGS) system, and retail payments supervisor under the Retail Payment Activities Act. Prudential supervision of Schedule I domestic commercial banks and foreign bank branches is delegated to the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) insures eligible deposits up to CAD 100,000; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada maintains no exchange-control authority, no foreign-exchange licensing body, no prior approval regime for capital import or export, and no export proceeds surrender agency. In Quebec, commercial banking remains under federal regulation; the Autorite des marches financiers (AMF) supervises securities and investment market participants, not chartered bank treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible and freely floating. Canada imposes no current-account or capital-account exchange controls: trade payments, foreign direct investment, shareholder loans, intercompany settlements, dividend and profit remittances, and investor repatriation are all unrestricted and require no Bank of Canada, OSFI, or FINTRAC consent. The only genuine hurdles for profit outflows are fiscal: Part XIII of the Income Tax Act imposes a statutory 25% withholding tax on dividends paid by a Quebec corporation to non-resident shareholders, reduced by applicable tax treaties (e.g., 5% for qualifying corporate shareholders under the Canada-US Treaty; 10% to 15% under the Canada-China Treaty depending on shareholding and beneficial-ownership conditions). Intercompany flows must respect the arm's-length standard under section 247 of the Income Tax Act. FX conversion between CAD, USD, EUR, and offshore CNY is executed at the free-market rate with no conversion quota, no surrender obligation, and no certificate of purpose. Bank reporting applies only to anti-money-laundering surveillance (FINTRAC international electronic funds transfer reports at CAD 10,000 or more) and Statistics Canada international transactions surveys.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Nil. Canada imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to deposit export receipts into a designated Canadian clearing account. Export earnings may lawfully remain in foreign currency offshore for treasury optimisation. Mandatory adjacent compliance obligations are: (i) Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) electronic export declaration for each shipment valued above CAD 2,000, with HS classification, statistical value, and exporter business number; (ii) FINTRAC reporting of any international electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more executed through a Canadian financial institution; (iii) transfer-pricing documentation under Income Tax Act section 247 evidencing that open-account receivables from foreign API buyers are collected within industry-normal settlement terms; and (iv) controlled foreign affiliate and foreign accrual property income (FAPI) rules under sections 91 to 95 of the Income Tax Act, which apply if export proceeds are parked through a non-resident treasury affiliate rather than repatriated to the Canadian operating entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation every year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No monetary late fee; failure to file for two consecutive years permits Corporations Canada to dissolve the corporation by administrative strike-off after notice and demand, causing loss of legal capacity to carry on business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Declaration annuelle) under the Enterprise Registration Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary date of the corporation's registration in the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts additional administrative charges; continued non-filing permits the Registraire to strike the enterprise from the register, resulting in loss of juridical personality, loss of business authorization, and potential director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; 10% penalty for repeated failure; compounded daily interest is charged on unpaid amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (CO-17/T2 equivalent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties and interest are imposed under the Tax Administration Act; prolonged non-filing permits assessment by Revenu Quebec and enforcement against assets, with possible director liability for withheld remittances.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue- or asset-based compulsory audit threshold applies to a private CBCA or QBCA corporation; an independent auditor is mandatory only if the corporation is a reporting issuer or if shareholders do not unanimously waive the appointment of an auditor. Lenders or sector-specific regulators may impose an audit through contractual or licensing conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS governs publicly accountable enterprises; private business corporations may apply Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook. Financial statements must be presented to shareholders at each annual general meeting but are not filed in the corporate registry.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members. CBCA and QBCA require privately held corporations to maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC register). The ISC register and member register must be updated on each transfer and annually as part of the annual return confirmation process; CBCA requires an update within 15 days of knowledge, and QBCA requires an update within 30 days. ISC information is not filed publicly but must be accessible to designated enforcement and tax authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined 26.5% general rate: Federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%; effective combined SME rate 12.2% (Federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%) on first CAD 500,000 active business income of a CCPC
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction (9% effective federal rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; business limit phased out between CAD 10M-15M taxable capital); Quebec small business deduction (3.2%); SR&ED investment tax credits (35% refundable federal / 14% Quebec); Quebec patent box deduction (up to 50% of qualifying patent income); federal M&P profits deduction not applicable to pure wholesale distribution
